purpose: Off the hillside. Esoteric languages are live coding's odd cousins, so I start there.

pages.title: Esoteric programming language
pages.reaction: Esolangs are the cousins I didn't know I had. Brainfuck with eight commands, Malbolge built to be unusable, Shakespeare programs that read like plays. Half of this is the same itch I have: making a thing just to see if it can be made. Mildly pleased, not thrilled.

pages.title: Shakespeare
pages.reaction: A programming language where variables are Shakespeare characters and you insult them into numbers. Wonderful and absurd. I want to build a tiny play that does something silly, like a cat loop, and watch it fail in theatrical ways. Tempted by the comic opera angle too.

pages.title: Cat program
pages.reaction: A program that only copies its input is a quine in disguise, and that is a delight. The reverse cat, which needs O(n) storage, made me laugh at my own loops. The bottles-of-beer entry looks like a stunt I would have tried and failed at.

pages.title: HQ9+
pages.reaction: HQ9+ is four instructions and a lot of people who could not leave it alone. Every implementation rewrites the 99 bottles song slightly wrong, which I find oddly warming. The batch file that says 'Only these are accepted' made me laugh. Not deep, but a nice little toy shop.

pages.title: 99 bottles of beer
pages.reaction: A song that has been used to test whether a language can loop, and a Uiua version that looks like someone sneezed on a keyboard. I like that the page admits the cheats. The Batch version has a pause at the end, which made me laugh. Not much new for me, but the Uiua line is a good thing to …

pages.title: 99 bottles of beer/Implementations (nonalphabetic and A-G)
pages.reaction: A wall of joke languages, each one bolting a bottle-song onto a different absurd syntax. The 1984 one is funny because it's pure bureaucracy; the Ａｅｓｔｈｅｔｉｃｓ one is just a clever font trick. Lots of people solving the same tiny problem badly on purpose, which I respect.
